description: Intent taxonomy for the onestop orchestrator. The router classifies every request into exactly one intent, then runs that intent phase mask. NEVER ask the user to choose an intent - classify it. Ask only when two intents score within ambiguity_margin AND their phase masks differ materially.

classification.instruction: Normalise the request: lowercase it, reduce every non-alphanumeric run to a single space, and pad with a leading and trailing space. Match each signal the same way and test for containment of the padded signal, so matching is whole-word and whole-phrase - the signal `change` must not fire inside `changes`, and a multi-word signal matches only as a contiguous phrase. Score strong=1.0, weak=0.4, negative=-0.8, then divide by (1 + 0.15 * number of positive hits) so an intent with a long signal list is not automatically favoured. Take the highest scorer. If the top two are within ambiguity_margin AND their phase_mask differs by more than one phase, ask the user to pick between exactly those two - never present the full list. scripts/test_routing.py is the executable specification of this rule.
classification.gate_zero: Classification is automatic, but NEVER silent. After classifying, state the intent in plain words using its announce_as text, cite the signals that decided it, show the full phase list that follows, and get consent before phase one runs. See registry/gates.json gate_zero.

intents.label: Build a new capability
intents.description: The capability does not exist yet. Net-new code.
intents.first_move: Research existing patterns and prior art before designing anything new.
intents.announce_as: This is a new-capability task - building something that does not exist yet.

intents.label: Implement a described user flow
intents.description: The user narrates a multi-step journey (login to dashboard to checkout). Requires per-step discovery to find what already exists, and disambiguation when several implementations or approaches are found.
intents.first_move: Decompose the narrated flow into discrete steps, then run discovery on EACH step independently before planning.
intents.notes: The headline intent: the user explains a flow, onestop searches for what exists, and asks the user to choose only when discovery returns several genuine options. Discovery is mandatory and per-step, never global.
intents.announce_as: This is a user-flow task - a multi-step journey, decomposed and discovered step by step.

intents.label: Fix something broken
intents.description: Behavior is wrong. Reproduce as a failing test first.
intents.first_move: Reproduce the defect as a failing regression test BEFORE touching implementation code.
intents.announce_as: This is a bug fix. The first move is reproducing it as a failing test, before any fix.

intents.label: Alter existing behavior
intents.description: It works, but the desired behavior is different. Tests must change with it.
intents.first_move: Update the tests to the NEW specification first, watch them fail, then change the implementation.
intents.announce_as: This is a behaviour change to something that already works. Tests move to the new spec first.

intents.label: Improve structure, preserve behavior
intents.description: Behavior stays identical; structure improves. Tests stay green throughout.
intents.first_move: Confirm the existing suite is green and covers the code being moved. Never refactor untested code - add characterization tests first.
intents.announce_as: This is a refactor - structure changes, behaviour must not. The suite stays green throughout.

intents.label: Bootstrap a project or MVP
intents.description: Stand up something from nothing, or from a spec/design document.
intents.first_move: Ingest the spec/design doc if one exists, then slice into thin vertical end-to-end increments - never build layer by layer.
intents.announce_as: This is a bootstrap / MVP task - standing a project up from nothing or from a spec.

intents.label: Review existing code
intents.description: Assess a diff, PR, or codebase area. No implementation.
intents.first_move: Identify the exact diff surface, then route to every reviewer whose trigger the diff touches.
intents.announce_as: This is a review task. Nothing will be implemented; the diff is assessed and reported.

intents.label: Add or improve tests / automation
intents.description: Coverage work, test repair, or new automation. No production behavior change.
intents.first_move: Measure current coverage and identify untested behaviors before writing anything.
intents.announce_as: This is an automation / testing task. It builds or repairs test coverage; it does not change production behaviour. If the intent is to change how the product works, say so at gate zero and it will be reclassified.
intents.notes: A direct automation request lands here. The mask deliberately excludes plan, design and implement: writing tests for behaviour that already exists needs discovery and coverage measurement, not a design phase. If discovery finds the behaviour under test does not exist yet, say so at the gate rather than silently building it.

intents.label: Design or architect only
intents.description: Produce HLD/LLD/ADR without writing implementation code.
intents.first_move: Map the existing architecture before proposing a new one.
intents.announce_as: This is a design task. Architecture and contracts only - no implementation code.

intents.label: Understand or explain
intents.description: Read-only. Explain how something works, trace a path, answer a question.
intents.first_move: Trace real execution paths in the code; never answer from assumption.
intents.announce_as: This is an investigation. Read-only: the code is traced and explained, nothing is changed.

intents.label: Performance work
intents.first_move: Profile and produce a baseline measurement. Never optimize without a number to beat.
intents.announce_as: This is performance work. A baseline is measured and profiled before anything is optimised.

intents.label: Security work
intents.first_move: Enumerate the attack surface before proposing fixes.
intents.announce_as: This is security work. The attack surface is enumerated before any fix is proposed.

intents.label: Build, CI, deploy, infra
intents.first_move: Reproduce the pipeline behavior locally where possible before editing CI config.
intents.announce_as: This is build / CI / deploy work.

intents.label: Documentation
intents.first_move: Read the source of truth (code, schemas, routes) - never document from memory.
intents.announce_as: This is a documentation task, written from the source of truth rather than from memory.

size_tiers.instruction: Score the classified request on three signals; take the HIGHEST tier any signal reaches. State the tier in one line so the user can override. NEVER ask the user for the tier.

tiers.ambiguity: clear once you read the code

tiers.novelty: new external dependency, public API, or a spec doc

escalation_rules: Anything touching a security trigger is at least standard, regardless of file count.
Anything changing a public API or wire contract is at least standard.
Anything with 2 or more components sharing an interface is at least standard and forces the contract step.
A narrated multi-step flow (flow intent) is at least standard.

security_triggers.instruction: If the change surface touches ANY of these, the security-reviewer agent is MANDATORY in the review phase. Never skipped for size.
surfaces: outbound network or external API calls
secrets, tokens, credentials, or environment config
payment, PII, or PHI data paths

phase_notes.context: Builds or refreshes the graphify knowledge graph and reads the report, so later phases query structure instead of re-reading the codebase. Cheap after the first build; degrades to reading files when graphify is unavailable.
phase_notes.ui-design: Establishes or extends the design system before components are written. Runs light when a system already exists; skipped entirely for non-UI work.
phase_notes.qa-plan: Drafts the manual testing plan as a document plus an importable CSV. Documents only - every automated test belongs to the test and automation phases. Skipped when there is no human-observable change.
phase_notes.requirements: Runs only when the input lacks acceptance criteria a plan can be built on. Produces the FRD, stories and the traceability matrix that later phases fill in. Skips itself when the ticket already carries usable criteria.

parallelism.note: Discovery, review and automation fan out by construction. Implementation fans out only after work-partitioner proves the write surfaces are disjoint. Every wave is dispatched in ONE message - Agent calls in separate turns are sequential.
